data.name: Sample - Microsoft Graph API (fork) - 3.1.0
data.description: Sample playbooks for the "Microsoft Graph API (fork)" connector. If you are planning to use the sample playbooks in your environment, ensure that you clone those playbooks and move them to a different collection, since the sample playbook collection gets deleted during connector upgrade and delete.

workflows.name: Respond to Compromised User Report
workflows.description:
One playbook for the "a user may be compromised" report: it checks Entra ID Protection for the reported account, asks a human to approve the response through a Microsoft Teams approval card, and on approval revokes the user's active sessions and blocks the reported source IP by appending it to an IP named location in Conditional Access. Both outcomes write a close-out comment on the security alert that carries the report, so the trail ends in the alert, not in someone's inbox.
Why best-effort on the risky-user lookup: this connector ships for tenants down to M365 Business Premium, where Identity Protection is P1 - the riskyUsers surface can be empty or refused while the rest of the response still makes sense. The lookup therefore runs with errors ignored and the playbook ends cleanly when it returns nothing actionable.
Inputs: approver (Teams recipient for the approval card; a conversation id or a user UPN the microsoft-teams connector can resolve - default soc-oncall@contoso.example), reported_ip (the source IP to block; default 198.51.100.7), named_location_name (the existing IP named location the IP is appended to - default "Lab blocked ranges"; the op appends to an EXISTING location, it does not create one), alert_id (the Graph security alerts_v2 id to comment on - default is the sample alert id). Outputs: outcome (contained, contained_no_block, not_approved or no_action_taken), risk_user, revoked, blocked_ip, named_location.
Live prerequisites: the connector's app registration needs User.RevokeSessions.All, IdentityRiskyUser.Read.All (P1) and Policy.Read.All plus ConditionalAccess... (the ipNamedLocation PATCH is covered by Policy.Read.All) - and the IP named location must already exist. Run it from a schedule for the sweep variant, or from the Execute menu with the report details.

arguments.named_location_name: {{ vars.input.params.named_location_name | default(vars.named_location_name, true) | default('Lab blocked ranges', true) }}

arguments.risk_user: {{ ((vars.steps.List_Risky_Users.data.value | default([], true)) | selectattr('riskState', 'equalto', 'atRisk') | list | first | default(none, true)).userPrincipalName | default('unknown@contoso.example', true) }}
arguments.risk_level: {{ ((vars.steps.List_Risky_Users.data.value | default([], true)) | selectattr('riskState', 'equalto', 'atRisk') | list | first | default(none, true)).riskLevel | default('unknown', true) }}
arguments.risk_summary: {{ ((vars.steps.List_Risky_Users.data.value | default([], true)) | selectattr('riskState', 'equalto', 'atRisk') | list | first | default(none, true)).userPrincipalName | default('the reported user', true) }} is flagged atRisk (risk level {{ ((vars.steps.List_Risky_Users.data.value | default([], true)) | selectattr('riskState', 'equalto', 'atRisk') | list | first | default(none, true)).riskLevel | default('unknown', true) }}) in Entra ID Protection.

groups.name: Note: List Risky Users
groups.description: Best-effort by design: ignore_errors keeps the run alive when the tenant answers 403/404 for identityProtection (no P1 license, missing scope) - the decision below treats that as "nothing actionable".

groups.name: Note: Pick Risky User
groups.description: The sweep can return several at-risk users; the approval card names the first one and the response targets exactly that account. A report about a specific user passes that user in the report and the sweep confirms it is flagged.

groups.name: Note: Revoke Sessions
groups.description: revokeSignInSessions kills every refresh/access token issued so far; the user must re-authenticate, which evicts an attacker holding a stolen session cookie.

groups.name: Note: Block IPs
groups.description: Appends the reported IP to the named location's ipRanges - existing ranges are preserved, so repeated reports accumulate in one location.

groups.name: Note: Close Out No Block
groups.description: The no-block branch still comments: sessions were revoked (the containment that matters most), but the IP could not be blocked and a human should create or fix the named location.

groups.name: Note: Contained No Block
groups.description: Same containment minus the IP block: the close-out comment carries the "why" for the auditor.

groups.name: Note: No Action
groups.description: Reached when the risky-user sweep returned nothing at risk (or the lookup itself was refused on this tenant) - a clean no-op, not a failure.

workflows.name: Purge Reported Phishing Mail
workflows.description:
Removes a reported phishing message from every mailbox the reporter listed. search_message looks the subject up per user, the run pauses for an approval card in Microsoft Teams showing exactly how many messages matched, and on approval del_message_bulk deletes the matched messages per user (the op's own thread pool deletes them in parallel). A close-out comment on the reported alert records how many deletions succeeded and how many failed, so a partial purge is visible instead of silent.
The matched-message list is built by a small Python snippet (the connector's del_message_bulk wants {user_id, message_id} pairs and the search result pages carry them one level apart). A page that answered with a Graph error body instead of a message list is skipped, not fatal - one broken mailbox must not stop the purge of the others.
Inputs: approver (Teams recipient for the approval card - default soc-oncall@contoso.example), phishing_subject (the exact subject to match; the op filters on subject eq), user_list (comma-separated UPNs to sweep - default alice@contoso.example, bob@contoso.example), alert_id (the Graph security alerts_v2 id to comment on). Outputs: outcome (purged, purged_with_errors, not_approved or no_mail_found), deleted_count, error_count, targets.
Live prerequisites: Mail.Read (search) plus Mail.ReadWrite (delete) on the mailboxes in user_list - application permissions with an application access policy, or delegated with consent per mailbox.

arguments.phishing_subject: {{ vars.input.params.phishing_subject | default(vars.phishing_subject, true) | default('Action required: payroll update', true) }}
arguments.user_list: {{ vars.input.params.user_list | default(vars.user_list, true) | default('alice@contoso.example, bob@contoso.example', true) }}

conditions.condition: {{ (vars.steps.Search_Mail.data.Message_Found_List | default([], true)) | map(attribute='value') | map('default', [], true) | sum(start=[]) | length > 0 }}

steps.name: Approval
steps.description: The subject search matched messages in {{ vars.steps.Search_Mail.data.Total_Users_Processed | default(0, true) }} mailbox(es) reported for the sweep. On approve the matched messages are deleted per user with del_message_bulk (each deleted message stays recoverable in the mailbox's Deleted Items). On reject nothing is deleted and the alert records that the purge was not approved.

schema.title: Approve purge of '{{ vars.phishing_subject }}' mail?
schema.description: The subject search matched messages in {{ vars.steps.Search_Mail.data.Total_Users_Processed | default(0, true) }} mailbox(es) reported for the sweep. On approve the matched messages are deleted per user with del_message_bulk (each deleted message stays recoverable in the mailbox's Deleted Items). On reject nothing is deleted and the alert records that the purge was not approved.

params.comment: Phishing mail purge (approved): deleted {{ (vars.steps.Purge_Mail.data.Message_Deleted_List | default([], true)) | length }} message(s) matching "{{ vars.phishing_subject }}" across {{ vars.found_count }} matched message(s); 0 deletions failed.

Phishing mail purge (approved, partial): deleted {{ (vars.steps.Purge_Mail.data.Message_Deleted_List | default([], true)) | length }} message(s) matching "{{ vars.phishing_subject }}"; {{ (vars.steps.Purge_Mail.data.Error_List | default([], true)) | length }} deletion(s) failed and need follow-up (typically already-purged copies answering 404).
Phishing mail purge REJECTED at approval: no mail matching "{{ vars.phishing_subject }}" was deleted. The report stays with the analyst for follow-up.

routes.name: Close Out Partial -> Purged With Errors

groups.name: Note: Search Mail
groups.description: One threaded search per user in user_list; the op aggregates the pages into Message_Found_List / Message_Not_Found_List (a page that errored lands in the not-found list as an error body). Size caps the per-user page so one hoarded mailbox cannot flood the run.

groups.name: Note: Purge Mail
groups.description: One call per run: the op's own thread pool fans the pair list out per user, so "per user" is the op's job, not a loop here. Results are checked afterwards because a 404 (the copy was already gone - auto purge, user action) is a NORMAL outcome for phishing sweeps and must not fail the run.

groups.name: Note: Close Out Partial
groups.description: A partial purge is still a purge - the comment says exactly which deletions failed so a human can chase the stragglers (usually copies that were already gone).

groups.name: Note: No Mail Found
groups.description: Nothing matched the subject in any reported mailbox - the sweep ran, the answer is "already gone", and the alert says so through the run outcome rather than a comment.
